replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: Start with the standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a). Compute the discriminant (b² - 4ac). If positive, two real solutions; if zero, one; if negative, complex solutions. Plug values into the formula and simplify. This method works for all second-order equations with real coefficients.

Differentiate y = f(x) to get f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are candidates for stationary points. Plug each into f(x) to find corresponding y-values. Verify by second derivative test: if f''(x) > 0, local minimum; if < 0, local maximum; if 0, inconclusive. This identifies critical points of the function.
